incidents.vector: Active exploitation of two zero-day vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-83548 SSRF, CVE-2026-83549 command injection) chained for unauthenticated remote code execution on SMA 1000 remote-access gateways.
incidents.impact: Internet-facing edge devices fully compromised; SonicWall confirmed in-the-wild exploitation and urges immediate patching, password/TOTP resets, and re-imaging of appliances showing indicators of compromise.

incidents.vector: Breached a public API endpoint, then used autonomous AI agents to map the network, raid source repositories, harvest secrets-manager credentials, and hijack CI/CD pipelines and cloud AI infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Weeks of intrusion tradecraft compressed into under 10 hours using more than 50 MITRE ATT&CK techniques; root credentials and cloud keys seized as part of a ransomware extortion operation.

incidents.vector: External Teams chats and calls impersonating IT helpdesk staff trick users into granting remote sessions, then a silent MSI install stages a Node.js-based backdoor implant.
incidents.impact: Hands-on-keyboard operators conduct Active Directory reconnaissance, screenshot capture, and WinRM lateral movement toward domain controllers — a pattern consistent with pre-ransomware staging.

incidents.vector: Hackers broke into the company's Amazon Web Services infrastructure over roughly two weeks in December 2025 and exfiltrated patient records.
incidents.impact: More than 9.5 million people had names, Social Security numbers, medical and financial data exposed; scope disclosed to federal regulators this week.

incidents.victim: US federal agencies, telecoms, hospitals, financial institutions
incidents.attacker: China — state-contracted espionage operators (MSS and PLA customers)
incidents.vector: Commercial Chinese contractor ran a distributed vulnerability-scanning system and a covert relay network of compromised IoT devices to obscure the origin of state hacking traffic.
incidents.impact: DOJ seized domains and disrupted both platforms, which supported nearly a decade of targeting including federal agencies and the US Senate; third such Chinese botnet disruption since December 2023.

incidents.vector: Exploits poorly secured VPNs, internet-facing application flaws, and credentials stolen from business partners, then deploys custom ransomware, loader, RAT, and an EDR-killer tool.
incidents.impact: At least seven Russian victims hit with multimillion-dollar ransom demands; the group is assessed as a rebrand of an earlier pro-Ukrainian ransomware operation and also leaks stolen data.

incidents.victim: Russian charity fundraisers (Davayte, You Are Not Alone)
incidents.vector: Compromised a Stripe-WooCommerce payment integration used for online auctions in mid-August, accessing donor payment account data.
incidents.impact: Donor email addresses and partial card details exposed for supporters of Ukrainian civilians and Russian political prisoners — data that could enable prosecution of donors under Russian law.

incidents.vector: Commercial spyware delivered via a zero-click exploit (Pegasus) and via physical device access during police detention (NoviSpy variant).
incidents.impact: 14 people targeted including a member of parliament, the largest documented spyware wave in Serbia to date, coinciding with election-related protests.

incidents.vector: Exploited old, unpatched vulnerabilities in an ownCloud file-sharing deployment to gain initial access.
incidents.impact: Reactor databases, personnel records, and credential stores were stolen from the agency.

incidents.victim: US Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF)
incidents.vector: Breach of the agency's lawful-intercept (CALEA) system; a Russian-speaking ransomware group briefly published 6.3 GB of claimed stolen data.
incidents.impact: Published data reportedly included names, phone numbers, IP addresses of investigation targets and mobile forensic data; ATF has confirmed it is investigating the breach.

incidents.victim: idscan.net (suspected) / 153M+ US and Canadian license holders
incidents.vector: Year-long ongoing exfiltration from a US identity verification provider whose scanners are used by rental car firms, dispensaries, hotels, and retailers.
incidents.impact: Dark web service selling scans of 153M+ drivers licenses, including those of senior US officials; records grow by hundreds of thousands daily and the FBI has opened an inquiry.

incidents.vector: Intrusion into company servers with exfiltration of patient, employee, provider, and financial data; a Russia-based ransomware-as-a-service gang claimed the attack.
incidents.impact: Hospital operator of 27 facilities in 12 states is being extorted with threats to publish stolen data; a class action suit has already been filed.

incidents.vector: Exploitation of critical authentication-bypass flaw CVE-2026-82329 (CVSS 9.8) within days of disclosure to mint administrator tokens on exposed repository servers.
incidents.impact: Multiple threat actors enumerating users, credentials and federation topology; admin access to a central artifact repository enables software supply chain tampering downstream.

incidents.vector: Two-decade-old polymorphic file-infector botnet spread via network shares and removable drives, monetized through clipboard-hijacking cryptocurrency theft.
incidents.impact: CrowdStrike, DOJ, FBI, and European partners sinkholed the peer-to-peer network on Aug 31, isolating over 15,000 infected machines and severing the operator's control channel.

incidents.victim: Unnamed critical infrastructure and enterprise networks
incidents.vector: Compromised Cisco IOS XR routers, TACACS authentication servers, and management infrastructure with custom router malware, using them as vantage points into connected networks.
incidents.impact: Long-dwell credential harvesting, traffic capture, and cross-network access into high-value environments, with log tampering and firewall manipulation to hide activity.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to information systems at a subsidiary detected in mid-August 2026.
incidents.impact: Internal patient ID numbers for 1,400+ US records, identifying data for fewer than 50 patients, and provider/employee contact data exposed; no medical devices affected, per an SEC 8-K filing.

incidents.vector: OAuth consent phishing over a commercial messaging app, impersonating officials and journalists to trick targets into authorizing a malicious cloud application.
incidents.impact: Grants persistent, password- and MFA-resistant access to victims' email and files; FBI issued a public alert on the campaign, which dates to late 2025.

incidents.vector: Exploited a bug in the underlying Cosmos blockchain platform, the same flaw used against six other platforms the prior week.
incidents.impact: Attacker initially drained roughly $74 million in crypto tokens; about $68 million was clawed back and the Cosmos network halted activity pending fixes.

incidents.vector: 33-hour BGP hijack of part of Hetzner's address space, paired with a fraudulently obtained TLS certificate and a cloned website serving malicious Virtualizor updates.
incidents.impact: Web hosting providers who pulled updates during the window may be compromised; the victim could not log hijacked traffic, so the number of affected users is unknown.

incidents.victim: Government and diplomatic organizations in Romania, Spain, Türkiye
incidents.vector: Spearphishing with macro-enabled Word documents using diplomatic lures to deploy a lightweight batch-script backdoor that abuses legitimate webhook services for command and control.
incidents.impact: Sustained initial-access campaigns from September 2025 through April 2026 supporting Russian intelligence collection against European diplomatic targets, including Moldova-related material.

incidents.victim: Global buyers of ZBT white-label routers
incidents.vector: Backdoors embedded in factory firmware of white-label routers sold worldwide under many brand names, beaconing to manufacturer-controlled domains with root privileges.
incidents.impact: Estimated six-figure count of infected devices, including cellular routers in remote industrial deployments; newly purchased units still ship with the implant despite vendor patch claims.
